To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The genetic characteristics of disease genes and drug targets are important factors that affect drug activity and druggability.
the genetic characteristics of disease targets are important for drug discovery.
agents with multiple disease-associated target genes are more likely drug candidates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a systems chemical genetics-based drug discovery strategy for prioritizing agents targeting multiple/relatively reliable disease-associated genes as drug candidates.

the development of computational tools and methods for prioritizing chemical agents that are more likely to exhibit desired activities in genetic diseases, which can be used for drug repositioning and discovery.

the development of computational approaches for predicting the activity of chemical agents targeting multiple genetic diseases, and for identifying agents that have the greatest potential to be developed as drug candidates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
agents targeting multiple disease-associated genes are more likely drug candidates.
agents targeting multiple disease-associated genes have higher therapeutic potential than those targeting only one.
the genetic information of targets and diseases should be fully considered in the drug discovery process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

chemical agents targeting disease-associated genes are more likely active against diseases and thus more likely to be drug candidates, and that the more disease genes an agent targets and the stronger the genetic links between these genes and diseases are, the more active the agent is likely to be against these diseases.
the multi-targeted agents are more likely to be drug candidates.
chemical agents targeting disease-associated genes with multiple genetic links are promising drug candidates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prioritization of agents targeting multiple disease-associated genes can be a powerful strategy for drug discovery.
agents targeting multiple disease-associated genes are likely to have desired activity and thus should be prioritized in the drug discovery process.
the systems chemical genetics approach is a promising way to discover novel drugs.
